title: The High Burn Ridge

features.name: burnt-ridge-spine
features.desc-on-touch: The ridge itself, rising through ash-pale grass, charred at the crest where this year's fire reached. You can read the burn pattern like a hand written in charcoal.

features.name: scorched-tree-stand
features.desc-on-touch: Four eucalyptus trunks, blackened to mid-height, still standing. The higher country burns differently than the valleys below—hotter, quicker, leaving the deep roots to remember.

features.name: ash-drift-pool
features.desc-on-touch: A low place where ash has settled in layers—each fire a readable stratum. The country burns in cycles, and each cycle forgets the one before, but the ash remembers.

features.name: renewal-shoot
features.desc-on-touch: A young growth already pushing through the char, red-barked and urgent. The ridge teaches itself to burn and recover faster each cycle.

inscription: the ridge reads its own burning; each fire teaches the next fire how to burn differently here

file.name: HighCountry_BurnCycle_Records_1887-2024.txt
file.note: Overlapping accounts of fires at this altitude. Each observer sees a different pattern. The land burns in layers.
